methods.name: Hash map / set lookup
methods.summary: Remember what has been seen in a hash map or set so each complement, duplicate or index lookup is constant time.

methods.name: Frequency counting
methods.summary: Count occurrences with a counter or fixed-size array (or a canonical signature) and reason from the counts.

methods.name: Prefix sums
methods.summary: Precompute running totals so any range sum, count or xor is a subtraction; pair with a hash map to count subarrays that hit a target.

methods.name: Difference array
methods.summary: Record each range update at its two endpoints, then sweep once to apply every update.

methods.name: Sort then scan
methods.summary: Sort, often with a custom comparator, so the answer appears in order or the elements that matter become neighbours.

methods.name: Bucket / counting sort
methods.summary: Place values into buckets by value, frequency or digit to sort or group in linear time.

methods.name: In-place index marking / cyclic sort
methods.summary: Use the array as its own hash table: swap each value to its index or flip signs to mark what is present.

methods.name: Simulation
methods.summary: Carry out the process the statement describes, step by step, with careful bookkeeping.

methods.name: Enumeration / brute force
methods.summary: Try every candidate the small constraints allow, pruning only obvious waste.

methods.name: Matrix traversal
methods.summary: Walk a 2-D grid in a structured order: spiral, diagonal, rotation, transpose or in-place markers.

methods.name: Two pointers (opposite ends)
methods.summary: Move pointers inward from both ends, using sorted order or symmetry to discard one side at every step.

methods.name: Two pointers (same direction)
methods.summary: Advance two forward pointers to compact in place, merge sorted sequences or match a subsequence.

methods.name: Fast & slow pointers
methods.summary: Move one pointer twice as fast as another to detect a cycle, find a cycle entrance or locate the middle.

methods.name: Fixed-size sliding window
methods.summary: Slide a window of constant length, adding the entering element and removing the leaving one.

methods.name: Variable-size sliding window
methods.summary: Grow the right edge and shrink the left edge while maintaining a window invariant, to find the longest, shortest or count of valid windows.

methods.name: Stack
methods.summary: Keep pending items last-in-first-out to match brackets, evaluate expressions, undo operations or replace recursion.

methods.name: Monotonic stack
methods.summary: Keep a stack in increasing or decreasing order to find the next or previous greater or smaller element and the span it dominates.

methods.name: Queue / deque simulation
methods.summary: Process items first-in-first-out (or from both ends) to model rounds, streams and recent-history windows.

methods.name: Monotonic deque
methods.summary: Keep a deque ordered so the front is always the best value in the current window, giving O(1) window maximum or minimum.

methods.name: Binary search
methods.summary: Halve a sorted, rotated or otherwise monotonic search space to find a target or a boundary.

methods.name: Binary search on the answer
methods.summary: Binary search over candidate answers, using a monotonic feasibility check to decide which half to keep.

methods.name: Linked list pointer manipulation
methods.summary: Rewire next pointers to reverse, merge, split or splice lists, usually behind a dummy head.

methods.name: Tree DFS (recursion)
methods.summary: Recurse through a tree, combining results from subtrees or passing state down a root-to-leaf path.

methods.name: Tree BFS (level order)
methods.summary: Visit a tree level by level with a queue to reason about depth, width or each level's nodes.

methods.name: Binary search tree property
methods.summary: Use the left < node < right ordering to search, validate, or walk a BST in sorted (in-order) order.

methods.name: DP on trees
methods.summary: Return a summary of each subtree (and optionally reroot) so the optimum is computed bottom-up over the tree.

methods.name: LCA & binary lifting
methods.summary: Precompute 2^k ancestors to answer lowest-common-ancestor, k-th ancestor and path queries in logarithmic time.

methods.name: Trie
methods.summary: Store strings (or numbers bit by bit) in a prefix tree to answer prefix, dictionary and maximum-xor queries.

methods.name: Heap / priority queue
methods.summary: Keep the smallest or largest candidate on top for top-k, k-way merge, two-heap medians and event scheduling.

methods.name: Backtracking
methods.summary: Build candidates choice by choice, undoing each choice after exploring it, and prune branches that cannot succeed.

methods.name: Graph DFS / flood fill
methods.summary: Explore a graph or grid depth-first to mark components, detect cycles or collect reachable cells.

methods.name: Graph BFS
methods.summary: Explore by distance with a queue for unweighted shortest paths, multi-source spreading, 0-1 BFS or search over states.

methods.name: Union-find
methods.summary: Merge sets with path compression and union by rank to track connectivity as edges arrive.

methods.name: Topological sort
methods.summary: Order a directed acyclic graph by peeling zero in-degree nodes (Kahn) or by DFS finish time, detecting cycles on the way.

methods.name: Weighted shortest paths
methods.summary: Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford or Floyd-Warshall over weighted edges, often on an augmented state graph.

methods.name: Minimum spanning tree
methods.summary: Connect every node at minimum total cost with Kruskal (sorted edges and union-find) or Prim (a heap).

methods.name: SCC, bridges & Euler paths
methods.summary: Tarjan or Kosaraju for strongly connected components, low-link for bridges and articulation points, Hierholzer for Euler paths.

methods.name: Network flow & matching
methods.summary: Model the problem as max flow, min cut, min-cost flow or bipartite matching.

methods.name: 1-D dynamic programming
methods.summary: Define dp[i] from a few earlier states, as in climbing stairs, house robber, decode ways or word break.

methods.name: Knapsack DP
methods.summary: Choose items under a capacity or target sum: 0/1, unbounded and counting variants such as coin change and subset sum.

methods.name: Longest increasing subsequence
methods.summary: Quadratic DP or patience sorting with binary search for the longest increasing (or chained) subsequence.

methods.name: State-machine DP
methods.summary: Track a few named states per position (holding, sold, cooling down) and the transitions between them.

methods.name: Grid DP
methods.summary: Fill a table over grid cells from neighbouring cells, as in unique paths, minimum path sum and maximal square.

methods.name: Two-sequence DP (LCS / edit distance)
methods.summary: dp[i][j] over prefixes of two strings or arrays: longest common subsequence, edit distance, wildcard and regex matching.

methods.name: Interval DP
methods.summary: dp[l][r] over subarrays, splitting each range at every point, as in burst balloons and palindrome partitioning.

methods.name: Bitmask DP
methods.summary: Use a bitmask of chosen items as DP state for assignment, travelling-salesman and subset-partition problems.

methods.name: Digit DP
methods.summary: Count numbers up to a bound digit by digit, tracking a tight-to-bound flag and the property being counted.

methods.name: Multi-dimensional DP / memoized search
methods.summary: Memoize a recursion whose state has several parameters (index, count, remaining budget, last choice).

methods.name: DP optimization
methods.summary: Speed up a DP transition with a monotonic queue, prefix maxima, convex hull trick or divide-and-conquer optimization.

methods.name: Greedy
methods.summary: Make the locally best choice at each step, justified by an exchange argument or invariant.

methods.name: Interval merging & scheduling
methods.summary: Sort intervals by start or end, then merge, insert, count overlaps or pick a maximum non-overlapping set.

methods.name: Sweep line / events
methods.summary: Turn ranges into start and end events and sweep them in order, keeping an active count or set.

methods.name: Math & closed-form reasoning
methods.summary: Use formulas, digit manipulation, parity or an observation that removes the need for search.

methods.name: Number theory
methods.summary: GCD and LCM, primes and sieves, factorization, modular arithmetic and fast exponentiation.

methods.name: Combinatorics & probability
methods.summary: Count arrangements in closed form with binomials mod p, inclusion-exclusion or contribution counting, or compute expected values.

methods.name: Computational geometry
methods.summary: Points, lines, slopes, areas, convex hulls and distances.

methods.name: Game theory
methods.summary: Minimax over optimal play, winning and losing positions, Nim and Sprague-Grundy values.

methods.name: Randomized algorithms & sampling
methods.summary: Reservoir sampling, rejection sampling, shuffling and weighted random choice.

methods.name: Bit manipulation
methods.summary: XOR tricks, masks, shifts, bit counting and enumerating subsets with bits.

methods.name: String parsing & building
methods.summary: Tokenize, validate, convert and build strings character by character.

methods.name: String matching & hashing
methods.summary: KMP, Z-function, rolling hash and suffix structures for pattern search and repeated substrings.

methods.name: Palindrome expansion
methods.summary: Expand around each centre (or use Manacher) to find and count palindromic substrings.

methods.name: Segment tree & range queries
methods.summary: Segment trees (with lazy propagation), sparse tables or sqrt decomposition for range queries with updates.

methods.name: Binary indexed tree
methods.summary: A Fenwick tree for prefix sums with point updates, often over coordinate-compressed values to count inversions.

methods.name: Ordered set / sorted container
methods.summary: A balanced BST, TreeMap or sorted list for floor, ceiling, rank and ordered iteration under updates.

methods.name: Data structure design
methods.summary: Implement a class API by combining structures, as in LRU caches, iterators, rate limiters and custom maps.

methods.name: Divide and conquer
methods.summary: Split the input, solve the halves recursively and combine them: merge-sort counting, quickselect and recursive construction.

methods.name: SQL selection & filtering
methods.summary: SELECT with WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT and DISTINCT over a single table.

methods.name: SQL joins
methods.summary: Combine tables with inner, outer, self and cross joins.

methods.name: SQL aggregation
methods.summary: GROUP BY with COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX, filtered with HAVING.

methods.name: SQL window functions
methods.summary: RANK, ROW_NUMBER, LAG, LEAD and running aggregates over PARTITION BY windows.

methods.name: SQL subqueries & CTEs
methods.summary: Nested and correlated subqueries, common table expressions and recursive CTEs.

methods.name: SQL string, date & conditional functions
methods.summary: CASE, IF, COALESCE, string functions, date arithmetic and pattern matching.

methods.name: SQL data modification
methods.summary: UPDATE and DELETE statements that change rows in place.

methods.name: Pandas DataFrame operations
methods.summary: Select, filter, reshape, merge and aggregate pandas DataFrames.

methods.name: Closures & higher-order functions
methods.summary: Functions that capture state or wrap other functions: counters, memoize, once, compose, array transforms.

methods.name: Promises & async timing
methods.summary: Promises, timeouts, debounce, throttle, cancellation and limited parallelism.

methods.name: Objects, classes & JSON
methods.summary: Deep traversal, comparison and transformation of objects, prototypes, classes and JSON values.

methods.name: Thread synchronization
methods.summary: Coordinate threads with locks, semaphores, condition variables and barriers.

methods.name: Shell text processing
methods.summary: Process files with grep, sed, awk and other Unix tools.
